Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\), \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = (2)(5) - (-1)(1) = 11 \neq 0\), so \(A^{-1}\) exists.
\(\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), hence \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{11}\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(X = A^{-1}B = \dfrac{1}{11}\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{11}\begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}\).
Therefore \(x = -\dfrac{5}{11},\ y = \dfrac{12}{11}\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ a & a & 2a \end{bmatrix}\), \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}\).
Here \(|A| = a \neq 0\) (take \(a \neq 0\)).
From \(R_2 - 2R_1:\ (2x+3y+2z) - 2(x+y+z) = 2 - 2\) gives \(y = 0\).
The third equation \(ax + ay + 2az = 4\) gives \(x + y + 2z = \dfrac{4}{a}\), i.e. \(x + 2z = \dfrac{4}{a}\).
From the first equation with \(y=0:\ x + z = 1\). Subtracting, \(z = \dfrac{4}{a} - 1 = \dfrac{4-a}{a}\), and \(x = 1 - z = \dfrac{2a-4}{a}\).
Therefore \(x = \dfrac{2a-4}{a},\ y = 0,\ z = \dfrac{4-a}{a}\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & -1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 5 & -2 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\), \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\).
Eliminate: \((\text{eq}3 - \text{eq}1):\ -y + 2z = -6 \Rightarrow y = 2z + 6\).
Substitute in eq1: \(5x - (2z+6) + 4z = 5 \Rightarrow 5x + 2z = 11\).
Substitute in eq2: \(2x + 3(2z+6) + 5z = 2 \Rightarrow 2x + 11z = -16\).
Solving \(5x + 2z = 11\) and \(2x + 11z = -16\): \(51z = -102 \Rightarrow z = -2\), then \(x = 3\) and \(y = 2(-2)+6 = 2\).
Therefore \(x = 3,\ y = 2,\ z = -2\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = (2)(1) - (3)(3) = -7 \neq 0\).
\(\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(A^{-1} = -\dfrac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(X = A^{-1}B = -\dfrac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = -\dfrac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix} -14 \\ 21 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}\).
Therefore \(x = 2,\ y = -3\).

Write \(AX = B\) with \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\) (equations: \(x+y+z=-1,\ y+z=2,\ x+y-z=3\)).
From eq1 \(-\) eq2: \(x = -1 - 2 = -3\).
From eq1 \(-\) eq3: \((x+y+z) - (x+y-z) = -1 - 3 \Rightarrow 2z = -4 \Rightarrow z = -2\).
Then eq2: \(y + (-2) = 2 \Rightarrow y = 4\).
Therefore \(x = -3,\ y = 4,\ z = -2\).

Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
Apply \(R_2 \to R_2 - 2R_1\) and \(R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6 & -7 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\).
Apply \(R_3 \to R_3 - 6R_2:\ 5z = 5 \Rightarrow z = 1\).
Then \(y - 2z = -1 \Rightarrow y = 1\), and \(x - y + z = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1\).
Therefore \(x = 1,\ y = 1,\ z = 1\).

Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ \tfrac{5}{3} \\ \tfrac{4}{3} \end{bmatrix}\) (equations: \(x+y=1,\ y+z=\tfrac{5}{3},\ z+x=\tfrac{4}{3}\)).
Adding all three equations: \(2(x+y+z) = 1 + \dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{4}{3} = 4\), so \(x + y + z = 2\).
Then \(z = 2 - (x+y) = 2 - 1 = 1\), \(x = 2 - (y+z) = 2 - \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), \(y = 2 - (z+x) = 2 - \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).
Therefore \(x = \dfrac{1}{3},\ y = \dfrac{2}{3},\ z = 1\).

Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 8 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
Eliminate \(y\): \((\text{eq}1 + \text{eq}3):\ 5x - 3z = 2\); \((\text{eq}2 + 2\,\text{eq}1):\ 5x + 5z = 10 \Rightarrow x + z = 2\).
From \(x = 2 - z\) in \(5x - 3z = 2:\ 5(2-z) - 3z = 2 \Rightarrow 8z = 8 \Rightarrow z = 1\), so \(x = 1\).
Then eq1: \(2(1) - y + 1 = 1 \Rightarrow y = 2\).
Therefore \(x = 1,\ y = 2,\ z = 1\).

Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 3 \\ 5 & 5 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 10 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\).
Apply \(R_2 \to R_2 - 3R_1:\ -4y = -8 \Rightarrow y = 2\).
Apply \(R_3 \to R_3 - 5R_1:\ -9z = -27 \Rightarrow z = 3\).
Then eq1: \(x + 2 + 3 = 6 \Rightarrow x = 1\).
Therefore \(x = 1,\ y = 2,\ z = 3\).

Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
Apply \(R_2 \to R_2 - 2R_1:\ -y - 3z = -15 \Rightarrow y + 3z = 15\).
Apply \(R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1:\ -7y - 5z = -19 \Rightarrow 7y + 5z = 19\).
From \(y = 15 - 3z\) in \(7y + 5z = 19:\ 7(15 - 3z) + 5z = 19 \Rightarrow -16z = -86 \Rightarrow z = \dfrac{43}{8}\).
Then \(y = 15 - 3\cdot\dfrac{43}{8} = -\dfrac{9}{8}\), and \(x = 8 - 2y - z = 8 + \dfrac{18}{8} - \dfrac{43}{8} = \dfrac{39}{8}\).
Therefore \(x = \dfrac{39}{8},\ y = -\dfrac{9}{8},\ z = \dfrac{43}{8}\).

Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 2 & -3 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 5 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}\).
Apply \(R_2 \to R_2 - 3R_1:\ -11y - z = -13 \Rightarrow 11y + z = 13\).
Apply \(R_3 \to R_3 - 2R_1:\ -9y + 2z = -5 \Rightarrow 9y - 2z = 5\).
From \(z = 13 - 11y\) in \(9y - 2z = 5:\ 9y - 2(13 - 11y) = 5 \Rightarrow 31y = 31 \Rightarrow y = 1\), so \(z = 2\).
Then eq1: \(x + 3 + 4 = 6 \Rightarrow x = -1\).
Therefore \(x = -1,\ y = 1,\ z = 2\).

Let the three numbers be \(x, y, z\). The conditions give: \(x + y + z = 6\); adding \(3z\) to \(y\) gives \(y + 3z = 11\); and first \(+\) third \(=\) twice second gives \(x + z = 2y\), i.e. \(x - 2y + z = 0\).
Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 11 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((\text{eq}1 - \text{eq}3):\ 3y = 6 \Rightarrow y = 2\). Then \(y + 3z = 11 \Rightarrow z = 3\), and \(x + 2 + 3 = 6 \Rightarrow x = 1\).
Therefore the numbers are \(1,\ 2,\ 3\).

Let the cost of a pencil, a pen and a book be \(x, y, z\) rupees. The data give:
\(4x + 3y + 2z = 150,\quad x + 2y + 3z = 125,\quad 6x + 2y + 3z = 175\).
Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 150 \\ 125 \\ 175 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((\text{eq}3 - \text{eq}2):\ 5x = 50 \Rightarrow x = 10\).
Then \(3y + 2z = 110\) (eq1) and \(2y + 3z = 115\) (eq2). Solving: \(5y = 100 \Rightarrow y = 20\), and \(z = 25\).
Therefore a pencil costs Rs.10, a pen Rs.20 and a book Rs.25.

Let the three numbers be \(x, y, z\). The conditions give: \(x + y + z = 6\); thrice the third added to the first is \(x + 3z = 7\); three times the first added to the sum of second and third is \(3x + y + z = 12\).
Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 7 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((\text{eq}3 - \text{eq}1):\ 2x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 3\). Then \(x + 3z = 7 \Rightarrow z = \dfrac{4}{3}\), and \(x + y + z = 6 \Rightarrow y = 6 - 3 - \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}\).
Therefore the numbers are \(x = 3,\ y = \dfrac{5}{3},\ z = \dfrac{4}{3}\).

Let the three numbers be \(x, y, z\). The conditions give: \(x + y + z = 2\); twice the second added to first \(+\) third is \(x + 2y + z = 1\); five times the first added to second \(+\) third is \(5x + y + z = 6\).
Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((\text{eq}1 - \text{eq}2):\ -y = 1 \Rightarrow y = -1\). \((\text{eq}3 - \text{eq}1):\ 4x = 4 \Rightarrow x = 1\). Then \(z = 2 - x - y = 2 - 1 + 1 = 2\).
Therefore the numbers are \(x = 1,\ y = -1,\ z = 2\).

Let the amounts invested at 6%, 7% and 8% be \(x, y, z\) rupees. The data give:
\(x + y + z = 5000\); total income \(0.06x + 0.07y + 0.08z = 350\), i.e. \(6x + 7y + 8z = 35000\); and income of first two exceeds the third by 70: \(0.06x + 0.07y - 0.08z = 70\), i.e. \(6x + 7y - 8z = 7000\).
Adding the two income equations: \(12x + 14y = 42000 \Rightarrow 6x + 7y = 21000\); subtracting them: \(16z = 28000 \Rightarrow z = 1750\).
From \(x + y = 5000 - z = 3250\) and \(6x + 7y = 21000\): \(6(3250 - y) + 7y = 21000 \Rightarrow y = 1500\), so \(x = 1750\).
Therefore Rs.1750 at 6%, Rs.1500 at 7% and Rs.1750 at 8%.

Let the costs of a Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry book be \(x, y, z\) rupees. The data give:
\(x + y + z = 210,\quad x + 2y + z = 240,\quad x + 3y + 2z = 300\).
Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 210 \\ 240 \\ 300 \end{bmatrix}\).
\((\text{eq}2 - \text{eq}1):\ y = 30\). \((\text{eq}3 - \text{eq}2):\ y + z = 60 \Rightarrow z = 30\). Then \(x + 30 + 30 = 210 \Rightarrow x = 150\).
Therefore the Mathematics book costs Rs.150, the Physics book Rs.30 and the Chemistry book Rs.30.
